fatal_errors: The proposed heat-treatment intervention does not reconstruct modulation-period control of coherent, semicoherent, and grain-boundary-dominated interfaces.

The hypothesis assigns maximum blocking to coherent interfaces, whereas the target mechanism attributes stronger dislocation blocking to semicoherent interfaces containing misfit dislocations and easier transmission to coherent interfaces.
The proposed approximately 1000 K creep regime is incompatible with the target room-temperature nanoindentation regime.
The cited evidence does not establish the claimed moderate negative-misfit/coherent-interface mechanism in the specified FCC/BCC coating.
explanation: The response addresses creep in an FCC/BCC HEA and offers a testable comparison, explicit operating range, and falsification rule, so it is a conceivable alternative hypothesis. However, it misses the target material architecture, processing variable, testing conditions, governing interface state, and diffusion/interface-slip interpretation. Its experiment also changes interface coherency and grain-boundary serration simultaneously, preventing clean attribution of any improvement. E2 supports serrated boundaries in a compositionally and structurally different high-temperature HEA, while E1 discusses stress-dependent diffusion and dislocation mechanisms but does not support coherent interfaces, negative lattice misfit, or serration as the governing factor. Thus, the generic predicted improvement is plausible but only weakly evidenced and does not reconstruct the reported semicoherent-interface optimum.
